keyQuotes: How far apart are 'building an app' and 'running a profitable business'? Anyone who has built a product knows they are worlds apart.

The part about writing the app might only account for 5% of the total workload in a product's lifecycle. The remaining 95% is the truly challenging part: promotion, customer service, repeat purchases, and operations.

AI is a lever, not an engine. CodeFly is already a long enough lever; it can pry a single thought of yours into a complete business system. But there needs to be something on the other end of the lever.

mainPoints.explanation: The author points out from personal experience that writing code accounts for only 5% of the workload in a product's lifecycle, with the remaining 95% being business aspects like promotion, customer service, and operations. Vibe Coding only solves the former.
mainPoints.point: The core of a one-person business is 'running a profitable business,' not 'building an app.'

mainPoints.explanation: The product provides a one-prompt system for generating a complete backend, automatically creates promotional materials, and offers 24/7 AI customer service (supporting WeChat integration), covering the hardest parts of running a business.
mainPoints.point: CodeFly packages the 'foundation + promotion + support' business loop, lowering the infrastructure barrier for solo entrepreneurship.

mainPoints.explanation: AI is a lever, not an engine. It amplifies what you already have (e.g., insights into a specific group of people), but the ability to discover a business opportunity still depends on personal judgment.
mainPoints.point: Tools cannot solve the three core questions: 'what business to do,' 'who to sell to,' and 'how to find those people.'

oneSentenceSummary: Starting from how 'Vibe Coding' solves product creation, this article proposes that 'Vibe Business' is what one-person businesses truly need, and demonstrates the closed loop from a single sentence to a complete business system through the practical use of the 'CodeFly' product.
originalTitle: 一人公司转折点：从 Vibe Coding 到 Vibe Business
summary: The article first points out that AI tools (Vibe Coding) have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code, but what a one-person business truly needs is to 'run a profitable business,' not to 'own an app.' The author uses their own experience (Little Cat Flashlight) to illustrate that writing an app accounts for only 5% of the workload in a product's lifecycle, with the remaining 95% being business aspects like promotion, customer service, and operations. Subsequently, the article provides a detailed demonstration of using the 'CodeFly' product, starting from the prompt 'Create a social app for extroverted cats,' and sequentially completing the entire process: app generation (with built-in products, orders, users, and a data backend), automatic generation of promotional posters and copy by the business assistant, and deployment of an AI customer service agent (supporting WeChat integration). It also verifies the product's applicability in e-commerce scenarios (one-click publishing as a WeChat Mini Program). Finally, the author introduces the concept of 'Vibe Business,' considering CodeFly as the first concrete product in this track, but emphasizes that the three key questions—'what business to do,' 'who to sell to,' and 'how to find those people'—cannot be solved by tools and still require personal judgment and insight.
title: The Turning Point for One-Person Businesses: From Vibe Coding to Vibe Business
